title: Skills and SKILL.md
bridge: A skill is like a README for one task that the agent opens only when that task comes up. Except the agent decides when to open it from one short field, the description. So that field is the real API, and the body is read only after the agent chose to load it.
intro: Skills teach agents and people the same way of working: how to plan, how to verify, how to write a PR. This lesson writes a skill, a SKILL.md with frontmatter and a plain body, and packages it in a plugin. Then it lists the plugin in a marketplace, the shape of our private RhinoHealth/claude-plugins.

picture.caption: A skill lives in a plugin, and a plugin in a marketplace. The model reads a skill's body only when a task matches.

nodes.label: Claude Code on a laptop or a VM

steps.text: the skill folder sits inside the plugin's skills/ folder
marketplace.json lists the plugin by name and source
the marketplace is added and the plugin installed (or forced by managed settings)
at session start the model sees each skill's name, description and when_to_use
when a task matches, it loads the body; a references/ file only when the body points to it

sections.h: A skill is a folder with one file
p: Open fcp and look at .claude/skills/create-test-data/SKILL.md. It is a Markdown file that starts with a block between two --- lines. That block is the frontmatter: a few YAML fields about the skill. Everything after it is the body, written for whoever does the task.

Claude Code reads every skill folder it knows: the project's .claude/skills/, your ~/.claude/skills/, and the skills/ folder of each installed plugin. Here is the frontmatter of the first rhino-core skill, plan-and-grill, from G8-03.
sections.because: We put when to use the skill in the frontmatter, because the model reads only that part before choosing.

code.text:
---
name: plan-and-grill
description: "Use before writing code for a ticket or task: decide whether to ask the requester questions first, then write a one-screen plan with the definition of done, 3-5 checks including an edge case, the proof each check needs, an estimate, risks and what is out of scope."
when_to_use: "A Jira ticket, bug report or feature request is about to be built; the user says 'plan this' or 'grill me'; the task is big or vague."
argument-hint: "[Jira key or task description]"
metadata: { version: "0.1.0" }
---

notes.text: The frontmatter starts and ends with ---. Claude Code parses it as YAML.
name matches the folder name. The plugin CI checks that (G8-07).
description: what the skill does and when to use it, in one or two sentences. The model decides from this.
when_to_use is added to the description in the skill list: the phrases and situations that should trigger it.
argument-hint shows what to type after /rhino-core:plan-and-grill when a person calls it by hand.
Our own version field. The plugin's version is what makes laptops update, not this one.

sections.h: What the model sees, and when
p: At the start of a session the model gets a list: each skill's name with its description and when_to_use. The body is not loaded yet. When a task matches a description, the model loads that skill's body. The body then stays in context for the session.

This is called progressive disclosure: show the short part always, the long part only when needed. The docs cut description plus when_to_use at 1,536 characters in the list. Our plugin CI is stricter: under 600 characters, and it must say when to use the skill.

A skill can go deeper with files of its own, like references/grill-questions.md. The body says when to read them, so they load only for the tasks that need them. The docs advise keeping SKILL.md under 500 lines.

callout.text: A skill that never fires is worth nothing, and one that fires on everything costs context on every task. The description decides both, so write it like the description of an MCP tool (lesson p8-3).

p: The body is for the reader who is doing the task, model or person. Write the goal first, then the reasons, the signs to look for and a worked example. Calm words, no ALL-CAPS MUST. Lesson p12-4 is about this voice in depth.

Byte's playbooks, skills/<team>/SKILL.md in RhinoHealth/byte, are plain Markdown with no frontmatter at all. They are baked into Byte's image and given to its review prompt directly, so nothing has to decide whether to load them. A Claude Code skill needs the frontmatter, because Claude Code chooses which skills to load.
sections.because: We write goals, reasons and signs instead of a fixed rulebook, because strong models follow a reason better than an order.

code.text:
# plan-and-grill

Goal: agree what "done" means before any code, so the work is checked against the ask, not against itself.

## Ask first, or plan now?
Ask the requester first when the ticket is big, spans teams, or two readings would lead to different code. Signs:
no example, a vague verb ("improve", "support"), a screen with no states, a change to an API others use. A small,
clear fix (a typo, copy, one obvious bug) goes straight to the plan. For big tasks read references/grill-questions.md.

## The plan (one screen)
1. Done means: 1-2 sentences in the user's words.
2. Checks: 3-5, at least one edge case. Each says what it looks at (what the user sees, an API response, a row
   count) and its proof: a short video, screenshots at 760 and 1440, or text output.
3. Screen states for UI: empty, loading, error, long content.
4. Estimate, risks, and what is out of scope.

notes.text: One heading, the skill's name.
The goal in one sentence, with the reason after the comma.
A decision, not a rule: ask first, or plan now?
Signs to look for, so the reader can judge a ticket the skill never saw.
The deeper file loads only for big tasks. Small tasks never pay for it.
The plan's shape, in numbered steps: the same format Nova posts in Jira and Slack (G4).
Each check names what it looks at and the proof it needs.

sections.h: A plugin: a manifest and folders
p: A plugin is a folder that ships skills with their friends. Subagents go in agents/, slash commands in commands/, hooks in hooks/hooks.json and MCP servers in .mcp.json. Only the manifest, plugin.json, sits inside .claude-plugin/. Everything else sits at the plugin's top level.

The manifest's version matters. When a plugin sets a version, people stay on it until the version changes. So a change to a skill that does not bump the version never reaches anyone. G8-07's plugin CI fails a PR that changes plugins/

/ without a higher version.
sections.because: We give every plugin a version, because the version is what makes laptops and agent VMs pick up a change.

notes.text: The plugin's name, in kebab-case. Its skills are called as be-guild:<skill>.
The name people see in the /plugin menu.
Semantic version. Bump it on every change, or nobody receives the change.
One line about what is inside, for the menu and for reviewers.
Where the source lives: the private marketplace repo.
Tells claude plugin eval where this plugin's eval cases live (lesson p12-3).

sections.h: A marketplace: one catalog for everyone
p: A marketplace is a git repo with .claude-plugin/marketplace.json, a catalog of plugins. G8-01 creates RhinoHealth/claude-plugins as a private repo. RhinoHealth/agent-skills is public and holds customer SDK skills, so our R&D plugins need their own home.

Plugins in this repo are listed by folder name under metadata.pluginRoot. Plugins from other repos, like kb in rnd-kb-tooling, are pinned by commit SHA. So a bump is a PR here and passes this repo's CI. Versions live only in each plugin.json, never in the catalog too.

There are two channels. The stable branch is what everyone gets. A second catalog, rhino-latest in channels/latest/, follows main. A change is promoted by fast-forwarding stable after a week on latest with green nightly evals.
sections.because: We keep one catalog in one private repo, so people and agents install the same tested tools from the same place.

code.text:
// RhinoHealth/claude-plugins/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json: the "rhino" catalog; everyone reads it at ref "stable"
{
  "name": "rhino",
  "description": "Rhino Health R&D plugins for Claude Code: shared skills, hooks and evals for people and agents",
  "owner": { "name": "Rhino Health R&D" },
  "metadata": { "pluginRoot": "./plugins" },
  "plugins": [
    { "name": "rhino-core", "source": "rhino-core", "category": "core",
      "description": "Plan and grill, verify, PR story, the task skills and safety hooks for every engineer" },
    { "name": "fe-guild", "source": "fe-guild",
      "description": "Frontend codebase skill, ticket-to-PR and PR review for fcp/frontend" },
    { "name": "be-guild", "source": "be-guild",
      "description": "Backend codebase skill, module guides and the BE planner for cloud, client and sdk" },
    { "name": "devops-guild", "source": "devops-guild",
      "description": "Infrastructure and gitops codebase skill, infra-change and security-fix" },
    { "name": "fcp-lab", "description": "Boot and drive a local FCP stack",
      // fcp-local-lab moves into the org in G0 (Nave); confirm where the plugin sits inside that repo
      "source": { "source": "github", "repo": "RhinoHealth/fcp-local-lab", "sha": "<40-char sha, bumped by PR>" } },
    { "name": "kb", "description": "Search and cite the R&D brain (RhinoHealth/rnd-kb)",
      "source": { "source": "git-subdir", "url": "https://github.com/RhinoHealth/rnd-kb-tooling.git",
                  "path": "plugin", "sha": "<40-char sha, bumped by PR>" } }
  ]
}

notes.text: The catalog is named rhino, so plugins are installed as <plugin>@rhino. Everyone reads the stable branch.
The owner field is required by the format.
pluginRoot lets a plugin's source be a bare folder name under ./plugins.
rhino-core: the skills every engineer gets, from this repo.
A plugin that lives in another repo: a github source pinned by a full commit SHA.
git-subdir: the plugin is one folder (path) inside another repo, again pinned by SHA.

p: A person adds the catalog once, then installs: /plugin marketplace add RhinoHealth/claude-plugins#stable, then /plugin install rhino-core@rhino. A repo can ask for it too. G8-02 adds extraKnownMarketplaces and enabledPlugins to fcp's .claude/settings.json, so contributors get the guild plugins after trusting the folder.

G8-02 also moves fcp's agents/fe-guild and agents/be-guild skills into the fe-guild and be-guild plugins. Skills that only make sense inside fcp stay in fcp/.claude/skills: create-test-data, the backend test runners and add-nvflare-version. Cross-references change to the plugin namespace, for example be-guild:be-module-cloud.
For a whole company, asking people to install is not enough. Lesson p12-2 forces rhino-core onto every laptop with managed settings.

callout.text: To try a plugin without installing it, start a session with claude --plugin-dir ./plugins/hello. It loads for that session only and changes none of your settings.

quiz.q: Which part of a skill does the model read before it decides to load the skill?

options.text: The name and description (with when_to_use), from the frontmatter
options.why: Only that short part is in the session's skill list; the body loads after.

options.text: The whole body, so it can judge whether the skill fits
options.why: Loading every body would fill the context on every task; that is what progressive disclosure avoids.

options.text: metadata.version, to pick the newest skill
options.why: Our version field is for people and CI; it plays no part in choosing a skill.

quiz.q: You fixed a sentence in rhino-core's verify skill and merged. A week later laptops still show the old text. Why?

options.why: There is no such cache rule; updates follow the plugin's version.

options.text: The plugin's version in plugin.json was not bumped, so Claude Code saw no update
options.why: With a version set, people stay on it until it changes. G8-07 fails PRs that forget.

options.text: The marketplace.json also needs the new version
options.why: Versions live only in plugin.json; the catalog never repeats them.

quiz.q: Why do our R&D plugins live in a new private repo, RhinoHealth/claude-plugins?

options.text: Because Claude Code cannot read public marketplaces
options.why: It can; the official Anthropic marketplace is public.

options.text: Because plugins must live inside fcp
options.why: Plugins live in their own repo so every repo and every agent gets the same copies.

options.text: Because RhinoHealth/agent-skills is public and holds customer SDK skills, and R&D tools are internal
options.why: G8-01: a private repo, read for engineering, write for Platform and the guild leads.

words.plain: A folder with a SKILL.md that teaches one task; the model loads it when its description matches.
The YAML block between two --- lines at the top of SKILL.md: name, description, when_to_use and more.
Show the short description always, the body when the task matches, deeper files only when needed.
A folder with .claude-plugin/plugin.json that ships skills, agents, commands, hooks and MCP servers together.
A git repo with .claude-plugin/marketplace.json listing plugins people and agents can install.
A branch of the marketplace: stable for everyone, latest (main) for people trying changes first.

tickets.why: Creates the private marketplace repo with the rhino catalog, the stable channel and SHA-pinned outside plugins.
Moves fcp's FE and BE skills into the guild plugins, each with a plugin.json, and registers the catalog in fcp.
plan-and-grill is the first rhino-core skill: frontmatter that fires on the right tasks and a plain body.
Plugin CI validates every manifest with --strict, checks frontmatter and fails PRs without a version bump.

remember: The description decides when a skill loads, the version when people get it, and the marketplace where they get it from.
